subject: English
passage: Between 1948 and 1961, labor historian Robert Gallagher recorded hundreds of interviews with factory workers on reel-to-reel tape and wax cylinders, media that most modern playback equipment cannot read. An archival transfer initiative is now working to ______ these recordings so that the testimonies remain available to scholars such as Owen Barrett, who studies mid-century union organizing.
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Choice A is the best answer. In this context, 'salvage' means to rescue or recover something threatened with loss. The passage explains that Gallagher's interview recordings are stored on reel-to-reel tape and wax cylinders that most modern equipment cannot read, putting the material at risk of being lost. A transfer initiative working to 'salvage' these recordings is one working to rescue them from obsolete media so that scholars like Owen Barrett can continue to use them.
